q: Alcohol is assessed by which sensation?
opts: Warmth at the back of the mouth and throat
exp: The burn is the clue, and it is easily confused with body. Very high alcohol also reads slightly sweet.

q: Why is tannin best assessed after several sips rather than one?
opts: It fades with repetition, so the first sip overstates it
The first sip is always inaccurate whatever is being judged
exp: Astringency builds as saliva proteins are stripped, so a single sip understates it. A wine that seemed supple can turn firm by the third mouthful.

q: Confusing tannin with acidity is a common error. What distinguishes them?
opts: Tannin dries the mouth; acid makes it water
Tannin is sweet; acid is bitter
Tannin is felt only in white wine, where acid is absent
exp: Opposite physical responses, and while tannin is chiefly a red-wine component, acid is in every wine. Both can make a wine seem firm, which is where the confusion comes from.

q: Serving temperature affects perceived structure in which way?
opts: Temperature changes aroma but leaves structure untouched
Cold accentuates alcohol and warmth accentuates acid
exp: Warmth does the reverse, pushing alcohol and body forward. Much of what is blamed on a wine is really a service fault, and the useful range is narrower than most people assume.

q: A wine smelling of wet cardboard, damp cellar and muted fruit is showing what?
exp: TCA strips fruit before it announces itself, so a merely dull wine may be lightly corked. It can come from cellar materials as well as cork.

q: Nail varnish and vinegar on the nose indicate which fault?
exp: Acetic acid with ethyl acetate. Trace levels add lift and are sometimes deliberate; past a threshold the wine is spoiled.

q: Struck match, rubber or drains on opening, often blowing off with air, suggests what?
exp: Sulphur compounds from a low-oxygen environment. Decanting or swirling frequently clears it, which distinguishes it from a permanent fault.

q: A white wine that is deep gold, flat and smelling of bruised apple is likely what?
exp: Acetaldehyde and colour deepening. Deliberate in Sherry and Vin Jaune, a fault in an unfortified table wine.

q: A pushed-up cork and a maderised, stewed character point to what?
opts: Cork taint, which lifts the cork as it develops
Heat damage in storage or transit
Reduction from a ferment starved of oxygen
exp: Wine expands when it gets hot and forces the cork. It is a shipping and storage failure rather than a winemaking one.

q: Sparkling wine is generally served within which range?
exp: Cold holds the mousse and keeps the pressure manageable on opening. Fine vintage Champagne benefits from the warmer end.

q: Full-bodied red wine is best served around which temperature?
exp: Room temperature is a phrase from unheated houses. Above about 18 C alcohol dominates and the wine loses definition.

q: Beaujolais and other light reds are often served how?
exp: Low tannin and bright fruit take a chill well. Over-warm Gamay turns flabby.

q: Serving a white wine too cold has which effect?
exp: Aromatics need warmth to volatilise. An expensive white poured from an ice bucket is often tasted at its worst.

q: Which fortified wine is conventionally served chilled?
exp: Fino and Manzanilla are served cold and drunk fresh, closer to a white wine than to the other fortifieds.

q: Why is an ice bucket filled with both ice and water rather than ice alone?
opts: Without water the wine would freeze against the ice
Water conducts heat away far faster than air
Water in the bucket stops the label soaking off the bottle
exp: Ice alone touches only part of the bottle and leaves air in the gaps. Half water and half ice chills in a fraction of the time, at the cost of a soaked label rather than a saved one.

q: Why is a wine glass tapered inward at the rim?
opts: The narrower rim strengthens the glass against knocks
It makes the pour look larger
It concentrates aromas toward the nose
exp: A bowl that narrows gathers the volatiles. It is also why a glass is filled to its widest point and no higher. A fine rim is the most fragile part of the glass, not the strongest.
